title: Everyday Sexism
author: Laura Bates
target_audience: Students and researchers of gender studies and sociology
Activists and advocates against gender discrimination
General readers seeking awareness about sexism and social justice
People affected by or interested in understanding sexism in daily life
core_themes: Prevalence of sexism in everyday life
Structural and systemic nature of gender discrimination
Impact of sexism on women and girls across ages and backgrounds
The normalization and invisibility of everyday sexism
Importance and power of sharing personal experiences
Need for social and cultural change
primary_purpose: To document and highlight the pervasive, varied, and often overlooked forms of sexism experienced by women and girls, giving a collective voice to their stories and challenging society to acknowledge and address these issues.

structure_format.narrative_style: First-person and third-person; anecdotal and analytical
structure_format.organization: Organized into thematic chapters (workplace, education, public spaces, media, etc.), each exploring manifestations of sexism through real stories and supporting analysis
features: Firsthand testimonies sourced from the Everyday Sexism Project website
Discussion of relevant cultural and historical context

key_concepts_lessons: Sexism is experienced by women of all ages, backgrounds, and professions, often beginning in childhood.
Many forms of sexism are so normalized that they go unremarked and unchallenged.
Sharing personal experiences, even online, can build solidarity and challenge isolation.
Sexism manifests in various spheres: workplace, education, media, public spaces, relationships, and more.
Recognizing patterns in everyday sexism is the first step toward meaningful societal change.
Men and boys also have a role in challenging and dismantling sexist structures and attitudes.
notable_features: Draws from over 50,000 submissions to the Everyday Sexism Project
Blends personal stories with social analysis
Accessible style aimed at a broad audience
Catalyzed further activism, projects, and policy conversations
cultural_historical_context: Launched as a website in 2012 and published as a book in 2014, 'Everyday Sexism' arrived during a global resurgence in feminist activism, marking the importance of digital platforms in social movements. The project influenced wider public conversations and helped spark similar projects and discussions worldwide.
reception_impact: Widely praised for giving a platform to everyday experiences of sexism
Credited with influencing policy debates and media discussions on gender equality
Translated into multiple languages and used as an educational resource
Some critics have questioned the book’s anecdotal approach, but it is broadly recognized as a landmark in feminist literature
Helped foster online and offline communities supporting gender equality
comparable_titles: Men Explain Things to Me by Rebecca Solnit
The Equality Illusion by Kat Banyard
We Should All Be Feminists by Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
Invisible Women: Data Bias in a World Designed for Men by Caroline Criado Perez
